code_needs: Tests: LevelDataM2Tests.PlayOrder and the count; a replay step for level25 at Normal and Difficile (0 discoveries, explained samples > 0), modelled on ProbeTestsM7LevelsC.

Audit (recommended, small): a 'decoy' necessity check, i.e. re-run the search with every same-kind decoy removed and require 'aucun horaire'. Today the audit only forces at least one explained sample (World.NeedDecoy) and never proves the decoys are needed. Until it exists, prove it by hand with a variant file without decoys.
Audit (recommended): print the explained-sample count, the waiting share and the pause count (the numbers report notes the audit prints neither share nor pause count).
Optional: a night lighting preset (IDEAS ART1) would sell the night guard; the level works in day light, so it is not required.
Optional: a 'decoy' entry in LevelDef.Lessons with its audit check, so the card and the tests can name the rule.
levels.targets: Normal strict exit 45-70 s (Difficile solvable, at most +20 s). Waiting 25-40 % of the schedule, at least 6 pauses of 0.5 s or more, none above 6 s. Decoy-explained samples on the Normal schedule at least 40 (level 3 has 30, level 13 has 8). Decoy-free variant file: no schedule (or exit at least +50 %). At least two of the three lanes (south lane, boulevard, north lane) carry a valid schedule when the other two are blocked (variant files with a box prop across each lane). All 3 rooms used: stockroom = spawn + G6, booth = G0, hall = route. Budget at most 110/120 draw calls and 22/24 materials (small-level class, 3 rooms). Audit run under 60 s. Relaxed exit (R1b, when it exists) at least 65 % of strict. Rush counter-routes (straight dash at full speed; schedule with waits removed) lose.
risks: Budget: 3 rooms means the small-level budget (120 draw calls, 24 materials). 19 decoys = 38 draw calls; my estimate for the whole level is about 95. If the budget line exceeds 110, drop the new-arrival chairs first, then the lobby row; do not add rooms just to reach the house class (5 rooms) unless each hosts a guard station.

Seeded wander can give seeds with no schedule or a trivial one (the guard parked in the booth or the stockroom). The seed sweep is part of the job; if no seed meets the targets, switch Marcel to 'loop' over the same 7 stations in the order G0 G1 G5 G2 G3 G6 G4 and change the hint (it must not say 'at random').

The audit accepts a decoy within 0.6 m, while the chair can get no closer than about 0.49-0.51 m: a 0.1 m window. Level 3 works with the same 1.1 m spacing; keep the spacing exact and keep the slots on the 0.25 m grid where possible (the audit warns otherwise, see level 13).

Marcel walks 1.7 m/s and can turn a row end faster than a player reacts. Every row end has a slot within 1 m (sale rows at z 8.0, dining sets at z 2.25 / 3.95, lobby row at z 4.25), so a freeze is always close; if playtests show unfair catches, change him to 'default' (1.2 m/s, same 0.75 tolerance).

Nina is optional: remove her if the Normal exit exceeds 75 s or waiting exceeds 40 %. With two humans the audit requires them to share a room (both are in the hall) and stay 0.6 m apart (her stations are 4 m or more from Marcel's).
Two chair levels in a row (level25 then level24) share the body axis; allowed by rule 4 (they differ on threat, shape, exit and look), and the finale's 'chair from level 1' is deliberate.
Station walks between rows: rows are 0.45 m deep and bays 3.55 m wide, so every walk has 1.2 m or more of clearance except where decoys stand; check the audit's NavMesh walk notes.
The review said 'thirty decoys': 19 to 23 is what the 120 draw call budget allows; the effect of 'thirty' comes from the slots (each pair of chairs gives one, about 35 legal freeze points).

LENGTH VERSUS THE PRD (2 to 6 minutes)
The PRD length can only mean a first clear including failures (feedback section 4): a clean 6 minute route would break the 8 s wait cap or be a walk. Targets here are strict-audit exits of 45-70 s (Showroom) and 60-85 s (finale, up from 40.4 s). With a 3 to 5 x retry factor for a new player, that lands in the 2 to 6 minute window. The length comes from beats, not floor: the finale route gets SHORTER (about 29-35 m against 39.5 m today, since the dead west rooms go) while its exit grows by 20-45 s through 8 or more pauses of 2-6 s, each a decision (Rex's back, Theo's glance, Mamie's glance, Lea's turn, the robot's pass).
